title: Introduce invocation echoes and alert timbre adjuster
author: Priya Menon
release_notes: Adds low-overhead 'invocation echoes' telemetry and an adaptive alert tuning component (alert timbre adjuster) that reduces rhythmic-burst false positives. Configurable via observability.timbre.* flags. No public API or DB schema changes.
description:
Context and motivation: Production alert noise has been dominated by periodic invocation bursts (prefetches, retries, client-side batching) that trigger token-cost and latency SLO alerts but are not actionable for customers. This PR introduces two complementary mechanisms to reduce false positives and improve root-cause signal-to-noise: 1) invocation echoes: a lightweight synthetic trace/span injected on a controlled sample of warm invocations to measure rhythmicity, kernel queue coupling, and cross-tenant echo strength; and 2) alert timbre adjuster: a pipeline component that computes a compact spectral/timbre score for invocation streams and uses it to scale or attenuate alert thresholds when high-frequency structure is detected.
Summary of changes:
- telemetry/tracing: add invocation echo span (invocation.echo) and a tiny header that propagates echo id; collect echo latency, kv-cache warm status, and microburst ordinal.
- metrics: introduce invocation.echo_strength{tenant,route}, invocation.timbre_score{tenant,route}, and invocation.timbre_band_power metrics (high/med/low).
- alerting pipeline: new filter stage that ingests timbre_score and applies a configurable attenuation function to SLO policies (exponential dampening by score).
- dashboards: new "Invocation Echoes" dashboard with heatmap of echo_strength vs route, timbre spectrogram panel, and before/after alert counts.
- config and rollout: feature flags observability.timbre.enabled and observability.timbre.canary_tenants; canary rollout plan included.
- tests: unit tests for spectral estimator, integration test simulating rhythmic bursts and verifying alert reduction, e2e smoke for tracing compatibility.
- docs: added docs/observability/invocation-echoes.md describing the mechanism, tuning knobs, and recommended canary plan.
Commits summary: [1] Add spectral estimator and timbre scoring core; [2] Emit invocation.echo span and header propagation; [3] Metrics plumbing and prometheus export for timbre bands; [4] Alert pipeline stage and attenuation config; [5] Dashboards and docs; [6] Tests and canary rollout scripts.
Changed areas (high level):
- src/telemetry/tracing/invocation_echoer.go
- src/telemetry/metrics/timbre_estimator.go
- src/alerts/pipeline/timbre_attenuator.go
- infra/prometheus/rules/timbre-metrics.rules.yaml
- dashboards/invocation-echoes.json
- docs/observability/invocation-echoes.md
- tests/telemetry/echo_integration_test.go
- configs/observability/timbre.example.yaml
- tests/telemetry/echo_integration_test.go
- configs/observability/timbre.example.yaml
- runbooks/observability/timbre_playbook.md
Implementation notes:
- Spectral estimator: lightweight, streaming FFT-ish estimator that keeps O(k) memory (k = number of bands, default 8). Tunable window length (default 30s) and sample rate (default 5s). Runs in the observability ingest tier; computation offloaded to a dedicated worker pool to avoid impacting request path.
- Echo injection: 0.1% sample by default, configurable per-tenant. Echo spans are tiny and emitted as child spans; they do not change response behavior.
- Alert attenuation: timbre_score is normalized 0..1 and plugged into alert threshold scaling: threshold' = threshold * (1 + alpha * timbre_score)^-beta. Default alpha/beta tuned after canary.
- Privacy and security: no PII added; echo ids are ephemeral and rotated per-window.
Performance: microbenchmark on canary cluster shows <0.5% CPU increase on ingest workers at default settings and 1.2% memory increase per worker for the estimator state.
Testing and rollout: initial canary enabled for 5% of traffic (us-west-2) for 48h, monitor false-positive rate, overall alert volume, and SLO degradation. If attenuation reduces actionable alerts but maintains SLO signal, widen to 25% then global.
Migration notes: no DB migrations, no schema changes to user-facing APIs.
Ops knobs: observability.timbre.enabled, observability.timbre.sample_rate, observability.timbre.window_s, observability.timbre.alpha, observability.timbre.beta, observability.timbre.canary_tenants.
Related work and references: ENG-924 investigating rhythmic burst-driven noise; ENG-987 earlier kernel queue telemetry.
Review conversation summary:
- Samir Patel: "Perf looks promising; can you quantify worst-case CPU overhead with timbre window=120s?" Priya Menon: "Added microbench with window=120s to PR comment; worst-case CPU observed ~1.9% on ingest worker under synthetic burst traffic; included as a test artifact. Also added a guard that caps estimator threads per node."
- Alex Chen: "Please add unit tests that assert no change to existing trace baggage propagation and that echo headers do not leak to logs." Priya Menon: "Added tests and a sanitizer in tracing middleware; updated docs to note header isolation."
- Morgan Lee: "How will this interact with Dedicated/private installs where observability is self-hosted?" Priya Menon: "Timbre estimator runs in the control plane ingest process. For Private installs we ship the estimator module and the attenuation stage is optional; added config example in configs/observability/timbre.example.yaml."
CI summary: unit tests, linters, integration tests, dashboards validation. Unit-tests: pass. Integration (simulated bursts): pass. Dashboard validation: pass. Lint: pass. Flaky tests: none after fixes.
Merge and post-merge actions: Squash-merged by Samir Patel after addressing comments. Post-merge: trigger canary rollout (automated via ops/rollouts/run_canary.sh), add alert suppression monitor and a short playbook entry in runbooks/observability/timbre_playbook.md. Rollback plan: disable observability.timbre.enabled or set alpha=0 to revert attenuation immediately.
Why this is different from previous approaches: previous PRs focused on token-level cost attribution and sampling heuristics. This PR specifically addresses rhythmicity by injecting synthetic, low-cost signals (invocation echoes) and applying spectral analysis to modulate alert sensitivity, which reduces noisy periodic alerts without hiding real regressions.
